title: Find Players With Zero or One Losses
summary: Given an array of match results, return two lists: one for players with no losses and another for players with exactly one loss, both sorted in increasing order.
statement: Given an array of match results, return two lists: one for players with no losses and another for players with exactly one loss, both sorted in increasing order. Only include players who have played at least one match.
constraints: Each match is [winner,loser], and every listed player has played at least once.
The first result row contains players with zero losses; the second contains players with exactly one.
Sort both rows in increasing order and omit players with two or more losses.
hints: Count losses while collecting every player appearing as either winner or loser.
Players absent from the loss counter have zero losses; a count of one selects the second group.
Filter the player set by loss count and sort each resulting row.
Every played participant enters the set, every loss is counted once, and the two exact count predicates match the requested categories.
editorial: Every played participant enters the set, every loss is counted once, and the two exact count predicates match the requested categories.

tests.explanation: Players 1,2,10 have zero losses, while 4,5,7,8 have exactly one.
Players 1,2,5,6 never lose; players 3 and 4 lose twice, so the second row is empty.
